meta.notes: Judgment hidden in useful advice. Has the bag; has the dated button book. No grief-unlocked confession: the book is evidence on request. Another woman's death is never a key.

threads.topic: That's a good bag, on your chair.
You keep a book of buttons.
threads.source: B20, S12. On request, on any date after. It does not need Mrs. Wiggins.

lo_b1.line: I was going to mend the strap.

lo_b1s.line: Sit, you're dripping. That coat has been let out by somebody who hated the coat. No. I'll do it when you bring it. Sit.

lo_b2.line: You know whose. Everyone knows whose. I had it on Saturday morning off the chair on our landing, where nobody leaves a good bag, and I said to myself the clasp wants doing. So I wrote the ticket. And then I stopped.

lo_b3.line: "Bag, clasp, off the chair, twentieth July." Purse is still in it. No keys. Nobody took a purse. So you can ask yourself what kind of a thief that is, and then you can ask me about your cuffs.

lo_k1.line: Every button that comes through that door, with who, since before you'd believe. People think it's thrift. It's so that when somebody tells me they never had a thing, I can tell them what colour.

choices.label: Anything on the twentieth of July?

lo_k1s.line: You don't have to think of a question. I can always use someone to hold the other end of a sheet.

lo_k2.line: Six in the morning, before I'd got my shoes on. You'd be surprised who can't wait.

lo_k3.line: Six C. For a glove. I wrote it down that morning. One pearl, and she wanted it matched by noon, and I had one near enough. It's the book I use.
